title: Finite-free coefficient extension respects compact-support composition and refinement
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and chosen uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For $n\geq1$ and ramification index $e$, put $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ and $B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L=\mathcal O_L/(\varpi_L^{en})$; equality means equality of ideals. Thus $B$ is finite free over $A$ [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Work on the ordinary small etale sites, and on their bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale realizations [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Put $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For a separated finite-type $h:V\to W$ write $P_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}$ for compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], $R=A,B$. Define $c_{h,M}:S_WP_{h,A}M\to P_{h,B}S_VM$ using a compactification $h=pj$: its proper constituent is the $p_B^*\dashv Rp_{*,B}$ transpose of $S(\varepsilon_{p,A})$ after the canonical pullback/tensor identification, and its open constituent is the canonical balancing identification $S j_!\cong j_! S$ [lem-coef-finite-direct-image, def-exchange-projection].
Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms. Let $\alpha_R:P_{g,R}P_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{gf,R}$ be the canonical composition comparison [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, thm-sf-comp-composition], constructed from proper direct-image composition, open extension and the normalized proper/open interchange. For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ the coefficient maps $c_h$ are natural isomorphisms, compatible with proper refinements of all chosen compactifications, and
$$c_{gf,M}\,S_Z(\alpha_{A,M})
=\alpha_{B,S_XM}\,P_{g,B}(c_{f,M})\,c_{g,P_{f,A}M}.$$
This is an equality of actual $B$-linear morphisms from $S_ZP_{g,A}P_{f,A}M$ to $P_{gf,B}S_XM$. It holds both on the ordinary etale bounded constructible finite-Tor categories and under their canonical proper/open pro-etale comparisons. For a proper refinement $w:c'\to c$ of a compactification of any $h$, write $r_{w,R}:P^{c'}_{h,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}P^c_{h,R}$ for its canonical comparison. The refinement assertion means explicitly
$$c^c_{h,M}\,S_W(r_{w,A,M})=r_{w,B,S_VM}\,c^{c'}_{h,M}.$$
No smoothness, orientation, or equality of coefficient-valued traces is part of this assertion.

source.place: Step 1, compatibility of the three purity constituents and normalized traces with finite coefficients; Step 3, finite coefficient-field extensions; agent-stated finite-free structural lemma underlying these compatibilities

proof.text: The finite extension datum gives a finite free A-algebra B by [lem-coef-finite-free-extension], and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes S_T=-\otimes_A^LB functorially on K-flat representatives. For every compactification h=p\circ j, [lem-trf-open-ctf] puts j_!M in the bounded constructible finite-Tor domain. The ambient finite-type schemes have a finite dimension bound by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; consequently [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] gives the required constructibility and Tor bound for the ordinary etale proper direct images, while [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] gives it for their pro-etale realizations. This applies to M, P_{f,A}M, P_{g,A}P_{f,A}M and every intermediate object below. On the pro-etale realization [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies etale-origin witnesses, so all scalar extensions and compact-support comparisons used below are defined on the stated domains.

source.place: Step 3, finite coefficient-field extensions; finite-free structural lemma underlying these compatibilities

proof.text: Fix a compactification h=p\circ j. For the proper factor p, the map obtained by transposing the A-counit after scalar extension is exactly the B-linear map c_{p,-}^{A\to B} of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], with B finite over A; it is a natural isomorphism on the domain certified in Step 1 (j_!M is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by [lem-trf-open-ctf], and the compactifying scheme has finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], so [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper] applies). For the open factor, apply [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] with coefficient ring A, open immersion j, and second factor the constant sheaf B. Since j^*B=B, its canonical map is S(j_!M)\cong j_!(S M). It is a map in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B): B is finite free over A by [lem-coef-finite-free-extension], so -\otimes_AB is termwise exact, preserves quasi-isomorphisms and is computed termwise on any representative, and the derived map is the termwise image of the sheaf identity j_!P\otimes_AB\cong j_!(P\otimes_AB), which is B-linear for the action of B on the second factor. Composing the proper transpose with Rp_{*,B} of this open balancing map is, by the definition in the statement, c_{h,M}; hence c_{h,M} is a natural isomorphism in the B-coefficient category. The pro-etale version is deferred to Step 8, where the comparison of these two named constituents is checked.

source.place: Step 1, compatibility of the three purity constituents and normalized traces with finite coefficients

proof.text:
Let c=(j,p) and c'=(j',p') be compactifications of h:V	o W and u:c'	o c a proper refinement, so u\circ j'=j and p\circ u=p'. The refinement comparison P^c_{h,R}	o P^{c'}_{h,R} is Rp_{*,R}(\alpha_{u,R}) followed by the direct-image composition identification Rp_{*}Ru_{*}\cong Rp'_{*}, where \alpha_u:j_!	o Ru_*j'_! is the proper/open comparison of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] (the specified map of def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison); it is invertible by that node, and r_{u,R} is its inverse. Write \chi for the counit-transpose coefficient maps and  eta for the open balancing maps of Step 2; the \chi_v of [lem-sf-proper-open-coefficient-refinement] is by its definition the same transpose of the scalar-extended counit as c_v^{A	o B} of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Apply [lem-sf-proper-open-coefficient-refinement] to K=M, which is bounded, with S_VM bounded since B is flat over A:
$$R_{u,B}( eta_{j'})\,\chi_{u,j'_!M}\,S(\alpha_{u,A,M})=\alpha_{u,B,S_VM}\, eta_{j}.$$
Apply Rp_{*,B} and precompose with \chi_{p,j_!M}. Naturality of \chi_p moves S(Rp_*\alpha_{u,A}) past \chi_p, and the composition identity \chi_{p'}=Rp_{*,B}(\chi_u)\circ\chi_{p,Ru_*-} of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] (its finite-Tor inputs supplied by Step 1) gives
$$c^{c'}_{h,M}\,S_W(r_{u,A,M}^{-1})=r_{u,B,S_VM}^{-1}\,c^{c}_{h,M}.$$
Inverting the two refinement comparisons gives c^c_{h,M}S_W(r_{u,A,M})=r_{u,B,S_VM}c^{c'}_{h,M}. The identity and transitivity clauses of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] then give the assertion for every proper refinement and for comparisons through common refinements.

source.place: Step 1, compatibility of the three purity constituents and normalized traces with finite coefficients; proper refinement compatibility

proof.text: Choose the compatible compactification triangle used to construct the composition comparison \alpha_R for X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ. In its normalized proper/open decomposition, the coefficient square for each proper-direct-image composition arrow is the composition identity in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], and the open-extension arrows satisfy the corresponding square by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]: since B is finite free over A, S is computed termwise, and both composites S(j_{2!}j_{1!}P)\cong(j_2j_1)_!(SP) are the termwise canonical identification of sections supported in the smallest open, so the square of the coherent composition isomorphism with the balancing maps \beta commutes on every representative. These are equations of B-linear maps; the finite-Tor inputs and all proper outputs are in the domain by [lem-trf-open-ctf], [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper], [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale], and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The middle proper/open interchange is treated separately in Step 5. Pasting the direct-image and open-extension squares with that interchange square gives the composition equation for this compatible choice of compactifications.

source.place: Step 1, compatibility of the three purity constituents and normalized traces with finite coefficients; geometric composition constituent

proof.text: The middle square of the compatible compactification triangle in the construction of \alpha_R by [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] is the Cartesian square with V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y, top open b, bottom open i, left proper r and right proper p, and the interchange used there is \gamma_Q of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. On D^+ that \gamma_Q and the map \Gamma_Q of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] have the same representative i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I on a bounded-below injective, hence K-injective, representative J with resolution k_!J\to I, through the same canonical sheaf identification; so they coincide, and since Q is Cartesian the mate normalization of the latter node applies. Write E_R:L_i^*R_{p,R}\to R_{r,R}L_b^* for the ordinary open-restriction exchange and \gamma_R:I_{i,R}R_{r,R}\to R_{p,R}I_{b,R} for this normalized interchange. The node [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] specifies \gamma_R as the I_{i,R}\dashv L_{i,R} mate of t_R^{-1}, where t_R=R_{r,R}(\eta_{b,R}^{-1})E_RI_{b,R}; hence t_RL_{i,R}(\gamma_R)=1 with the open unit inserted. The inverse-image coefficient square commutes on K-flat representatives because both paths send x\otimes b to the same pullback tensor. Applying the mate-pasting identities of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to that square gives, for N on the proper compactification,\n$$\chi_{r,L_{b,A}N}S_Y(E_A)\lambda_{i,R_{p,A}N}=R_{r,B}(\lambda_{b,N})E_BL_{i,B}(\chi_{p,N}).\tag{1}$$\nHere \chi is the counit-transpose from [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], \lambda is the scalar/pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] for the derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Thus the interchange calculation is an equality of B-linear arrows, rather than an untyped assertion that squares paste.

source.place: Step 1, compatibility of the three purity constituents and normalized traces with finite coefficients; normalized proper/open interchange

proof.text:
Continue the mate computation of Step 5 at N=I_{b,A}M. The open balancing map has the unit identity
$$S_V(\eta_{b,A,M}^{-1})\lambda_{b,I_{b,A}M}=\eta_{b,B,S_VM}^{-1}L_{b,B}(\beta_{b,M}),$$
obtained by transposing the defining balancing map of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. Substitute this identity into (1), use naturality of E_B, and use t_RL_{i,R}(\gamma_R)=1. After transposing under I_{i,B}\dashv L_{i,B}, both sides reduce to \chi_{r,M}; since the adjunction bijection is injective, this proves
$$R_{p,B}(\beta_b)\chi_{p,I_{b,A}M}S_{\bar Y}(\gamma_{A,M})=(\gamma_BS_V)I_{i,B}(\chi_r)\beta_iR_{r,A}.$$
This is exactly the scalar-extension square for the proper/open interchange \gamma, including the open units and the mate normalization. Combining it with Step 4 and the direct-image/open composition squares gives
$$c_{gf,M}S_Z(\alpha_{A,M})=\alpha_{B,S_XM}P_{g,B}(c_{f,M})c_{g,P_{f,A}M}$$
for the compatible compactifications. The finite-Tor inputs and the intermediate P_{f,A}M are covered by [lem-trf-open-ctf], [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper], [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale], and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type].

source.place: Step 1, compatibility of the three purity constituents and normalized traces with finite coefficients; geometric composition constituent

proof.text: For arbitrary chosen compactifications of f, g and gf, conjugate the equality of Steps 4–6 by the canonical comparisons from the compatible compactifications to the chosen ones. Step 3 moves each c through those refinement comparisons, while [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] says that the composition comparison \alpha is natural under the same comparisons and independent of the common refinement. Adjacent inverse comparisons cancel, yielding the displayed composition equation for the chosen compactifications. The proper direct-image outputs and their finite-Tor hypotheses in this conjugation are the ones supplied by [lem-trf-open-ctf], [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-nonproper], and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type].

source.place: Step 1, compatibility of the three purity constituents and normalized traces with finite coefficients; compactification independence

proof.text:
Let an input on the pro-etale site be given with an etale-origin witness. [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies each pro-etale compact-support candidate with the comparison pullback of its ordinary etale candidate. The exact tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives
$$
u_T^*(N\otimes_A^LB)\cong
u_T^*N\otimes_A^LB,$$
so scalar extension commutes with comparison pullback. The proper coefficient maps c_p and their composition identities transport through the counit-mate normalization [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] and the composite direct-image comparison [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. The open balancing maps transport through [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]; its compatibility with tensor comparisons is the explicit coherence of [lem-sf-comparison-open-tensor-coherence]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the same inverse-image square identifies the normalized pro-etale proper/open interchange with the pullback of the etale \gamma square from Steps 5–6. The compact-support composition comparison and its refinement coherence transport by [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence], while the named proper/open refinement arrows transport by [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization]. Therefore pulling back the ordinary-etale equations of Steps 2–7 gives the same natural-isomorphism, refinement, and composition equations for the finite constructible pro-etale realizations, as equalities of B-linear morphisms. The witnesses and domain hypotheses are supplied by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin].
